source_operations: Read-only; no edit, move, cut or generation.
verdict: The intended energetic letter/object motion and final title recovery are present. Shortening/reframing the awkward transitions is a practical option; temporary blur, separation and occlusion are permitted by C and are not blanket failures.
observations: Both title rows initially move strongly toward the left in sampled frames; the requested TITAN-left / SOLUTION-right opposition is not clearly realized.

Around 0.667-1.0 s a second readable TITAN coexists with departing fragments and a separate extra T. At 0.75 and 0.833 s the top visually reads T TITAN. This is an extra-copy artifact, not merely a foreground object covering a correct word.
At 1.25-2.0 s the full title reads TITAN / SOLUTION while the ribbon curls, multiple ring arcs sweep and the glass panel rotates through the foreground.

During roughly 2.25-3.75 s letters separate, rotate into depth and reassemble amid strong object motion. Unreadable fragments in this phase are principally intended transitions; these sampled frames cannot establish a one-to-one identity for every rotating glyph.
At 3.917-4.0 s the top I is still tilted like a slash while the other letters settle. This is a rotation/settling awkwardness, not a confirmed substitution with a slash character.
By the 4.083 s dense sample all 13 letters are recognizable as TITAN / SOLUTION. From the 4.25 s sample through 6.0 s samples the complete title is clearly recovered.

The final 5-6 s reading beat succeeds in sampled frames. The title settles while ribbon, ring and panel motion continue toward the image edges. The final scene is not a pixel-perfect replica of the starting plate, which is not required by the present use case.

suggested_windows.note: About 0.6 s of visible letter reassembly, followed by readable title plus continuing background motion. Brief unreadable transition remains intentionally.
Shorter awkward assembly lead-in, then roughly 1.9 s of readable title with moving objects. Does not preserve the initial opposing-row stunt.
At its first frame the I remains slightly tilted; it straightens by about 4.083 s. Strong background motion remains, but little typography motion is retained.

minimal_prompt_refinements: Specify exactly 13 existing letter objects, five in TITAN and eight in SOLUTION, with no new incoming copy while outgoing letters are still visible.
Compress the most scattered letter phase to roughly 0.5-0.8 s while retaining aggressive ribbon/ring/panel motion, rather than making the whole scene static.
Make all letters face front and complete their snap into the title in one coordinated reading beat; avoid leaving I edge-on after the other letters have resolved.
scope: Frame-based visual assessment: 25 samples at 0.25 s spacing, 12 targeted dense frames, and full-size checks at 0.75, 4.083 and 6.0 s. No native timed playback or audio listening; no audio-sync or all-frame visual guarantee.
